newsitem.title: USA: House panel asks Clinton help in locating Trie.
newsitem.headline: House panel asks Clinton help in locating Trie.

text.p: The head of the House of Representatives committee investigating foreign campaign contributions asked the Clinton administration and the Chinese government for help on Tuesday in obtaining evidence from a key figure in the case.

House Government Reform and Oversight Committee Chairman Dan Burton said he needed White House help in obtaining documents from Yah Lin "Charlie" Trie who was subpoenaed in February and is now believed to be in hiding in China.
Burton said in a letter to President Clinton that "very serious allegations" concerning Trie "require your assistance and that of the State Department in obtaining evidence."

In a letter to China's ambassador to the United States, Li Daoyu, Burton formally requested Beijing's help in locating Trie for "return to the United States or, at a minimum, his availability for questioning."

The Indiana Republican also asked the president to instruct Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to petition China for formal return of Trie to the United States for questioning or to make him available for a federal deposition.

Trie, a one-time Little Rock, Arkansas, restaurant owner and friend of Clinton's, is being investigated for possibly funnelling more than $1 million to the Democrats and the president's legal defence fund.

He disappeared before congressional committees could question him and is believed to be in China. NBC television last week broadcast an interview with Trie from Shanghai, although Trie declined to appear on camera.
Congress and the Justice Department are investigating allegations that foreign countries may have sought to influence the 1996 presidential and congressional elections with campaign contributions.
